# residue

> Reclaim your storage from Git worktrees, automatically and safely. residue removes a worktree only when nothing in it would be lost, whichever coding agent left it.

`scan`, `explain`, `remove`, the Mac app and `watch` all run the same checks, and only a `candidate`, where every check passed, is ever removed. Git does the delete, with `git worktree remove`, never `--force`. `residue restore` recreates a deleted worktree for 30 days, without its ignored files, and puts a trashed one back whole for 7 days; branches, commits and the stash always stay. A pass is not a guarantee, and age alone does not mean inactive.

residue removes linked worktrees that any tool, or you, left behind. It does not create worktrees and it does not merge branches: [Worktrunk](https://worktrunk.dev) does. [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees) sweeps only the worktrees it created. residue needs `git` 2.36 or later. Releases have binaries for macOS, Linux and FreeBSD; Windows is not supported.

## Install

- [Install script](https://residue.whiteheap.com/install.sh): `curl -fsSL https://residue.whiteheap.com/install.sh | sh` installs residue through Homebrew on macOS, the signed apt, dnf or pacman repository on Linux, or else the checksum-verified release archive. On macOS and Linux it then turns on automatic cleanup, whose removals delete without the trash (Automate cleanup, below).
- [Homebrew](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/whiteheap/residue/main/README.md#install): `brew install whiteheap/tap/residue` installs residue without automatic cleanup.
- [Install residue](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/whiteheap/residue/main/docs/installation.md): the install script's flags and how to undo it, the signed repositories, the release archives and `cargo install`.

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/whiteheap/residue/main/README.md): every command, what it deletes and keeps, and its limits.
- [Inspect a worktree](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/whiteheap/residue/main/README.md#inspect-a-worktree): `residue scan` and `residue explain PATH` report each linked worktree as `candidate`, `keep`, `unknown` or `stale`, and delete nothing.
- [What removal deletes, and what it keeps](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/whiteheap/residue/main/README.md#what-removal-deletes-and-what-it-keeps): after you type `yes`, `residue remove PATH` deletes the checked-out tracked files, every one committed, and the ignored entries that match a regenerable rule. It keeps the branch, every commit, the stash and every other worktree.
- [Restore a removed worktree](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/whiteheap/residue/main/README.md#restore-a-removed-worktree): `residue restore` lists the trash entries and removal records, newest first, and brings one back.
- [Automate cleanup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/whiteheap/residue/main/README.md#automate-cleanup): `residue watch` removes a worktree when its work landed, or when the disk is low and it has sat idle. These removals delete: they do not use the trash. See what it would remove with `residue watch --once --dry-run`, then turn it on with `residue service install`.
- [Mac app](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/whiteheap/residue/main/README.md#mac-app): residue in a window, `residue-macos.dmg`, in every release from 0.0.8 on, for macOS 13 or later. It is not notarized yet, so macOS blocks it the first time you open it: [First launch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/whiteheap/residue/main/README.md#first-launch) has the steps.
- [Command and configuration reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/whiteheap/residue/main/docs/reference.md): PATH search, `--json` fields, exit codes and regenerable rules.
- [Automate residue](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/whiteheap/residue/main/docs/automation.md): default folders, fetching, launchd, systemd and the idle clock.
- [Platforms and testing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/whiteheap/residue/main/docs/platforms-and-testing.md): what was run on each platform, and what was not.

## Source

- [whiteheap/residue](https://github.com/whiteheap/residue): the Rust source, under the MIT license.
- [Releases](https://github.com/whiteheap/residue/releases): the archives, with SHA-256 checksums and build-provenance attestations, and each release's notes.
- [Security policy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/whiteheap/residue/main/SECURITY.md): how to report a vulnerability privately.
